seo.meta_title: When Can You Say '너' in Korean? | Use Their Name Instead
seo.meta_description: AI translates casual 'you' as 너, but Koreans rarely say it unless the other person is much younger or a very close friend. Use their name instead.

ai_failure.situation: Texting a new acquaintance your age, after you've both agreed to speak casually: 'Did you eat?'
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Translates casual 'you' as 너: 너 밥 먹었어?
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 너 is used freely only toward children much younger than you, or with very close friends your age or younger. With anyone else — even in 반말 — it can sound blunt or rude. Koreans call the person by name instead.

natural_solution.rule: Say 너 only to a young child or a close friend who is your age or younger. Otherwise, even in casual speech, use their name (with 야/아) or drop 'you' altogether.

alternatives.context: Casual speech with a friend — call them by name instead of 너
Just drop 'you' when it's clear who you're talking to
Fine with a very close friend your age or younger

nuance: Korean doesn't need a word for 'you' most of the time, and when it does, names and titles do the job. 너 is the plain second-person pronoun, and it signals that the other person is clearly below you in age or that you're very close. Agreeing to speak 반말 with someone doesn't automatically make 너 okay: many people still prefer being called by name, and 너 from someone who isn't close can sound like the start of a fight. See also 당신, which has its own problems.
